extracted.intended_audience: participating jurisdictions, HOME program recipients, public housing authorities, owners/managers of HOME-assisted rental housing, HUD regulatory and legal stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and short-term implementation guidance for specific provisions of HUD's HOME Investment Partnerships Program final rule, including delayed effective dates, corrections to regulatory text, tenant protections, per-unit subsidy limits, underwriting requirements, green building exceptions, and applicability of immigration law. Useful for jurisdictions and owners implementing or complying with 24 CFR part 92 changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates and further delays
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendatory instruction 2 is effective April 20, 2025, and amendatory instruction 3 is effective October 30, 2025. As of April 17, 2025, the effective date for amendatory instruction 27 (revising 24 CFR 92.253) in the HOME Final Rule is further delayed until October 30, 2025. The effective date for the addition of paragraph (c) to 24 CFR 92.250 is delayed until the date described in the DATES section of this publication. The provisions of the HOME Final Rule that are not further delayed by this publication are effective as of April 20, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which amendatory instructions and specific regulatory changes take effect April 20, 2025 versus October 30, 2025. HUD is withdrawing the single amendatory instruction that attempted to delay part of a multi-part instruction and instead issues two separate instructions with different effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections to 24 CFR 92.3 (compliance/effective date updates)
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD is making technical changes to update the compliance and effective dates listed in 24 CFR 92.3 to account for the delay from February 5, 2025 to April 20, 2025. The compliance dates detailed in various paragraphs of 24 CFR 92.3 of the HOME Final Rule are being revised to April 20, 2026, to ensure participating jurisdictions have a 1-year compliance period, as originally described in the HOME Final Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific date replacements in FR Doc. 2024-29824: remove 'February 4, 2025' -> add 'April 19, 2025'; remove 'February 5, 2025' -> add 'April 20, 2025'; remove 'February 5, 2026' -> add 'April 20, 2026'. Corrections to 24 CFR 92.3 are effective April 20, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum per-unit subsidy amount (24 CFR 92.250(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The total amount of HOME funds that a participating jurisdiction may invest on a per-unit basis in affordable housing may not exceed the per-unit dollar limits established by HUD in accordance with section 212(e) of the Act. HUD will publish the per-unit dollar limits for the area in which the housing is located annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD will publish its methodology for determining maximum per-unit dollar limits through a publication in the Federal Register with the opportunity for comment. Participating jurisdictions must adhere to HUD-published per-unit limits unless an applicable exception applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underwriting analysis for homeowner rehabilitation loans (24 CFR 92.250(b)(3)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: An underwriting analysis of the homeowner's ability to repay the HOME-funded rehabilitation loan is required only if the loan is an amortizing loan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits the situations that trigger a required underwriting analysis—non-amortizing loans (e.g., deferred, forgivable) do not require the same repayment ability analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology change: 'downpayment assistance' to 'homeownership assistance' (24 CFR 92.250(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove the words 'downpayment assistance' and in their place add the words 'homeownership assistance' in paragraph (b)(4) of § 92.250.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textual amendment effective April 20, 2025; reflects HUD's chosen terminology for program activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green building standards exception to per-unit limits (24 CFR 92.250(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A participating jurisdiction may exceed the per-unit dollar limits described in paragraph (a) by up to 10 percent if the project meets one of the green building standards identified by HUD and published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit, quantified exception (+10%) tied to HUD-identified green building standards; HUD will publish the list/identification of qualifying standards in the Federal Register. The effective date for adding paragraph (c) is October 30, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenant protections and selection (24 CFR 92.253) — interim application
rubrics_metrics.description: The effective date for the HOME Final Rule's revisions to 24 CFR 92.253 is delayed until the date described in the DATES section of this publication. Notwithstanding this delay, HUD reminds owners that, pursuant to 42 U.S.C. 12755(b), they may terminate the tenancy or refuse to renew the tenancy of a person in HOME-assisted rental housing based on the grounds of a direct threat to the safety of the tenants or employees of the housing or an imminent and serious threat to the property, and owners are not required to provide 30 days' notice prior to the termination or refusal to renew where the action is in accordance with the requirements of State and local law and the requirements of 24 CFR part 92.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although revisions to 92.253 are delayed, statutory authority under 42 U.S.C. 12755(b) continues to permit termination/refusal to renew for direct/imminent threats in accordance with applicable law. Participating jurisdictions and owners should apply currently effective lease requirements and tenant protections unless and until the delayed revisions take effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of PRWORA (immigration eligibility and verification) to HOME grants
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD reminds HOME program recipients that grants must be administered in accordance with all applicable immigration restrictions and requirements, including the eligibility and verification requirements that apply under title IV of the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 (8 U.S.C. 1601-1646) and any applicable requirements that HUD, the Attorney General, or the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services may establish from time to time to comply with PRWORA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure program administration and beneficiary eligibility verification comply with PRWORA and any implementing guidance from HUD, DOJ, or USCIS; this is a continuing obligation despite delays to other HOME rule provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim reading of cross-references affected by delay
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent that cross-references refer to tenant selection preferences in 24 CFR 92.253(e) or to the tenant protections contained in the tenancy addenda referenced in 24 CFR 92.253, these references shall be read to refer to the tenant selection preferences in 24 CFR 92.253(d) and to the lease requirements and tenant protections in 24 CFR 92.253 that are currently effective, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This interim reading is intended to avoid inconsistencies across 24 CFR parts 91 and 92 while certain provisions' effective dates are delayed. HUD intends to correct cross-references, where necessary, in a subsequent rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: HUD will solicit further public comment on delayed provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to HUD's review and to allow further public comment, HUD will issue a separate Federal Register publication inviting public comment on the provisions of the HOME Final Rule detailed in this publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The delay is explicitly to allow time for additional review and public comment; stakeholders should monitor Regulations.gov and future Federal Register notices for the separate notice inviting comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citation and statutory bases
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority for part 92 continues to read: 42 U.S.C. 3535(d) and 12701-12839, 12 U.S.C. 1701x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the statutory authority underpinning the HOME program rule and amendments; useful for legal and administrative context when interpreting or challenging provisions.
